title: The Octopus Mind
context:
For most of the twentieth century, invertebrates were regarded as simple creatures driven by reflex. The octopus has done much to overturn that view. Its nervous system contains roughly five hundred million neurons, a number comparable to that of a dog, yet only about a third of them are located in the brain. The remainder are spread through its eight arms, which can taste, touch and, to a surprising degree, make decisions without waiting for instructions from the centre.

Laboratory studies have documented the animal's capacity for learning. In a well-known series of experiments conducted in Naples in the 1950s, octopuses were trained to avoid a white square by receiving a mild shock when they attacked it, and they learned to ignore it within a few trials. Later researchers showed that captive octopuses could unscrew jar lids to reach food, a task that some mammals find difficult. Several aquarium keepers have also reported that individuals recognise particular staff members and squirt water at those they dislike.

Such abilities seem all the more remarkable given the animal's lifestyle. Most octopus species live only one to two years, and mothers typically die shortly after their eggs hatch, so young octopuses never meet their parents. They cannot, therefore, learn by imitation, as many birds and primates do. Whatever knowledge they gain must come from personal exploration. Some biologists suggest that this solitary upbringing explains why octopuses are so curious, although the hypothesis remains difficult to test.

Camouflage provides further evidence of sophistication. An octopus can change the colour and texture of its skin in under a second, matching a background of coral, sand or weed. Curiously, octopuses are thought to be colour-blind, as their eyes contain only a single type of light-sensitive pigment. How they match colours so accurately is therefore unexplained. One proposal is that the skin itself contains light-detecting proteins, allowing it to sense its surroundings directly, but this idea has not yet been confirmed in living animals. Divers who film octopuses on the seabed have also recorded them carrying coconut shells and later assembling them into portable shelters, behaviour that some scientists describe as a form of tool use. Others prefer a narrower definition of the term, so the label remains debated, and the same disagreement surrounds many other claims about invertebrate minds.

The practical implications are beginning to attract attention. Engineers designing soft robots have studied octopus arms because they can bend at any point, unlike jointed limbs. A prototype gripper modelled on the arm was able to pick up fragile objects such as eggs without breaking them. Meanwhile, ethicists argue that evidence of complex cognition should change the way octopuses are treated: in 2022 the United Kingdom extended legal recognition of sentience to octopuses, alongside crabs and lobsters. Critics of intensive octopus farming say that such legislation does not go far enough.

questions.prompt: Scientists once believed that animals without backbones behaved mainly through automatic responses.
questions.why: Bài nói rõ động vật không xương sống từng được coi là 'driven by reflex'.
questions.quote: invertebrates were regarded as simple creatures driven by reflex

questions.prompt: An octopus has considerably more neurons than a dog.
questions.why: Bài chỉ nói số nơ-ron 'comparable' (tương đương) với chó, không phải nhiều hơn hẳn.
questions.quote: a number comparable to that of a dog

questions.prompt: Most of an octopus's neurons are located in its brain.
questions.why: Chỉ khoảng một phần ba nằm ở não; phần còn lại ở các cánh tay.
questions.quote: only about a third of them are located in the brain

questions.prompt: The arms of an octopus can take some decisions without input from the centre of the nervous system.
questions.why: Cánh tay 'make decisions without waiting for instructions from the centre'.
questions.quote: make decisions without waiting for instructions from the centre

questions.prompt: The Naples experiments were the first to test learning in any invertebrate.
questions.why: Bài không nói thí nghiệm Naples là thí nghiệm đầu tiên trên động vật không xương sống.

questions.prompt: In the Naples experiments, octopuses stopped attacking the unwanted object after a small number of attempts.
questions.why: 'within a few trials' được diễn đạt lại thành 'a small number of attempts'.
questions.quote: they learned to ignore it within a few trials

questions.prompt: Unscrewing a jar lid is a task that every mammal finds difficult.
questions.why: Bài chỉ nói 'some mammals' gặp khó; 'every' là từ tuyệt đối sai.
questions.quote: a task that some mammals find difficult

questions.prompt: Some aquarium keepers have noticed octopuses reacting differently to different members of staff.
questions.why: Bài ghi nhận chúng nhận ra nhân viên cụ thể và phun nước vào người chúng không thích.
questions.quote: recognise particular staff members and squirt water at those they dislike

questions.prompt: Octopuses in aquariums squirt water at visitors more often than at staff.
questions.why: Bài chỉ nhắc đến nhân viên; không có so sánh với khách tham quan.

questions.prompt: Young octopuses are usually looked after by their mothers.
questions.why: Mẹ chết ngay sau khi trứng nở nên con không bao giờ gặp bố mẹ.
questions.quote: young octopuses never meet their parents

questions.prompt: Octopuses learn mainly by copying other octopuses.
questions.why: Bài nói chúng không thể học bằng bắt chước mà phải tự khám phá.
questions.quote: They cannot, therefore, learn by imitation

questions.prompt: The deaths of mother octopuses after their eggs hatch are caused by exhaustion.
questions.why: Bài nêu hiện tượng nhưng không nêu nguyên nhân.

questions.prompt: Every biologist accepts that a solitary upbringing makes octopuses curious.
questions.why: Chỉ 'some biologists suggest' và giả thuyết 'difficult to test'; 'every' là sai.
questions.quote: Some biologists suggest that this solitary upbringing explains why octopuses are so curious

questions.prompt: An octopus can change the feel of its skin as well as its colour.
questions.why: Texture (kết cấu) cũng thay đổi cùng với màu sắc.
questions.quote: change the colour and texture of its skin in under a second

questions.prompt: Octopus eyes contain several different types of light-sensitive pigment.
questions.why: Mắt chỉ có một loại sắc tố nhạy sáng nên bạch tuộc được cho là mù màu.
questions.quote: their eyes contain only a single type of light-sensitive pigment

questions.prompt: Light-detecting proteins in octopus skin have been proved to exist in living animals.
questions.why: Ý tưởng này 'has not yet been confirmed in living animals'.
questions.quote: this idea has not yet been confirmed in living animals

questions.prompt: An octopus matches its background faster than a chameleon does.
questions.why: Tắc kè hoa không được nhắc đến trong bài.

questions.prompt: Octopus arms are of interest to robot designers because they can bend in any place.
questions.why: Kỹ sư nghiên cứu cánh tay vì nó 'can bend at any point'.
questions.quote: they can bend at any point, unlike jointed limbs

questions.prompt: A robot gripper based on an octopus arm can hold eggs without breaking them.
questions.why: Bài nêu rõ nguyên mẫu gắp được trứng mà không làm vỡ.
questions.quote: pick up fragile objects such as eggs without breaking them

questions.prompt: British law now gives octopuses the same protections as farm animals.
questions.why: Bài chỉ nói luật công nhận khả năng cảm nhận; không so sánh với gia súc.
